seo.meta_description: Toyota C-HR 2016-2023 import from Japan for NZ buyers. Hybrid and turbo grades explained, plus auction availability, trim checks and import process.
seo.og_title: Toyota C-HR 2016-2023 Import from Japan NZ
seo.og_description: Looking at a Toyota C-HR 2016-2023 import from Japan? We explain the hybrid and turbo model range, late-run grades, auction checks and NZ import process.

blocks.hero_subtitle: If you want a compact SUV that feels a bit sharper than the average small crossover, the C-HR is still a solid one to search for through Japanese auctions. For 2023, the important detail is that Japan was still selling the facelifted first-generation car, so the exact model code and grade matter more than the year badge on its own.
proof_points: Importing estimate provided before bidding, with compliance as part of the process
blocks.why_kiwis_buy: The hybrid C-HR suits buyers who want Toyota hybrid running costs in a smaller SUV body, while the turbo range gives you the option of 4WD on the right model code. It also helps that late-run cars still came in a proper spread of grades, so you can search for a simple S or G, or hold out for a GR Sport or Mode-Nero special edition if that is the shape and trim you want.
blocks.video_caption: A late-run C-HR is one of those cars where the details matter. If the video shows the cabin and rear seat area clearly, we can match that against the auction list and confirm whether it is a straightforward G grade or one of the more specific GR Sport or Mode-Nero versions.
blocks.main_usp_deep: The main draw with the C-HR is that it gives you two quite different versions of the same SUV. The 1.8 hybrid is the simpler choice for daily use, front-wheel drive only with Toyota's eCVT, while the 1.2 turbo range opens the door to NGX50 4WD cars if that matters more than hybrid economy. One useful detail a lot of buyers miss is that a 2023 import from Japan is still the original AX10 or AX50 series, facelifted from 2019, not the newer-shape C-HR sold elsewhere later on. That makes model-code checking important before you bid, because year alone does not tell you whether you are looking at ZYX11 hybrid, NGX10 turbo 2WD or NGX50 turbo 4WD.

buyer_persona.headline: Who is this car right for?
buyer_persona.body: This suits someone who wants a compact Toyota SUV but does not want to jump straight to a taller, boxier shape. It also works for buyers who are happy to choose carefully between hybrid economy and turbo 4WD rather than assuming every C-HR is the same underneath. If that sounds like you, this is a solid match.

car_specs_benefits.benefit: This is the front-wheel-drive hybrid setup used in ZYX10 and ZYX11 cars, so you get the familiar Toyota self-charging layout with no plug-in charging to think about.
If you want a C-HR with a bit more choice around drivetrain, this is the engine used in the turbo range, including the 4WD NGX50 models.
A 2023 car sits in the later facelifted part of the range, which helps narrow down trim and model-code checks when you are comparing auction cars.
That makes the hybrid choice straightforward. If you need four driven wheels, you are looking at the turbo side of the range instead.

car_specs_benefits.spec: Late-run grades include S, G, GR Sport and Mode-Nero Safety Plus III variants
car_specs_benefits.benefit: There is enough spread in the range to search by budget and equipment level, rather than treating every late C-HR as the same car.

standout_features_block.headline: Features that stand out
standout_features_block.intro: The exact equipment needs to be confirmed on the auction car, but these are the late-run C-HR features worth looking for when you shortlist one.

items.title: GR Sport trim
items.body: GR Sport matters because it is more than a badge in the late C-HR range. It is one of the top late-run grades and gives buyers a more specific version to search for when they want the sportier cabin and chassis-focused trim rather than a standard S or G.
items.image_hint: Front seats and steering wheel photographed from the open driver's door, focusing on sport-oriented trim details

items.title: Mode-Nero Safety Plus III editions
items.body: These special-edition cars sit higher up the late-run range and are worth searching separately because the naming changed across the production run. If one appears at auction, we will confirm the exact grade wording and listed equipment before you decide whether it suits your brief.
items.image_hint: Dashboard and front cabin shot showing trim finish, centre stack and any grade-specific interior detailing

items.title: Compact coupe-SUV packaging
items.body: The C-HR's shape is a big part of why people look for it. It gives you a higher driving position and SUV footprint without stepping into a larger family SUV, which suits buyers who want something easier to place around town.
items.image_hint: Rear three-quarter exterior shot showing the roofline, rear doors and compact SUV proportions in one frame

items.title: Clear grade spread across late-run cars
items.body: Late-run C-HRs were still offered in core S and G grades as well as GR Sport and Mode-Nero variants. That gives you a clearer shortlist by budget and trim level instead of treating every 2023 car as interchangeable.
items.image_hint: Front cabin and seats photographed to show trim level and equipment differences

tech_deep_dive_block.headline: Under the skin
tech_deep_dive_block.intro: The C-HR range makes more sense once you separate the hybrid and turbo cars properly.

items.title: 2ZR-FXE hybrid system
items.body: The hybrid C-HR uses Toyota's 1.8-litre 2ZR-FXE with an eCVT in ZYX10 and ZYX11 model codes. It is a self-charging hybrid, so the battery is topped up by the petrol engine and regenerative braking rather than a plug. Around town that means the handover between petrol and electric drive is handled automatically, with the eCVT keeping the car smooth in stop-start traffic. In this range, the hybrid is 2WD only, which is a useful shortcut when you are filtering auction cars.

items.title: 8NR-FTS turbo range
items.body: The other side of the C-HR line-up is the 1.2-litre 8NR-FTS turbo. In Japan this sits in NGX10 2WD and NGX50 4WD cars, paired mainly with CVT. The turbo option matters because it is the route into a 4WD C-HR if that is what you need. Some catalogue records also show a manual on certain NGX10 grades, so transmission needs to be confirmed on the exact car rather than assumed.

items.title: 2019 facelift and late-run model codes
items.body: Production ran from 2016 to 2023, with the facelift arriving in 2019. A late 2023 import still belongs to that same first-generation AX10 or AX50 family, which catches some buyers out because other markets moved on to a newer shape later. The practical takeaway is simple, check the model code first, then the grade, then the listed equipment. That is the cleanest way to avoid mixing up a ZYX11 hybrid with an NGX50 turbo 4WD just because both wear the same C-HR badge.

items.title: Outputs and grade ladder
items.body: Context sources report the 1.2-litre turbo at 85kW and 185Nm, and the 1.8 hybrid at 90kW system output. For late-run cars, the grade ladder runs from S and G through to GR Sport and Mode-Nero Safety Plus III variants, with ZYX11 G being a sensible all-round trim to target if you want simpler spec verification.

faq_block.q: Is a 2023 C-HR from Japan the newer-shape model?
faq_block.a: No. Japan kept the first-generation C-HR through to the end of production in 2023, so a 2023 import is still the facelifted AX10 or AX50 series car.

faq_block.q: What costs make up the import total?
faq_block.a: The main parts are Vehicle cost, Japan-side costs, Shipping costs, Customs clearance, Compliance and On-road costs. We put those into an importing estimate before you decide whether to bid.

faq_block.q: Can you tell me if a C-HR is typically within the entry requirements before bidding?
faq_block.a: Import viability must be checked for the exact model code and vehicle before bidding. Final certification happens in NZ after arrival and depends on the exact car and its documentation.

faq_block.q: How long does the process take?
faq_block.a: Timing depends on when a suitable car appears, whether your bid is successful, and the shipping schedule after purchase. We keep you updated through the process rather than guessing dates too early.

faq_block.q: What do you check on the auction car before I bid?
faq_block.a: We review the auction list information available for that vehicle, including the model code, grade, mileage, recorded condition notes and listed modifications. We also match the photos against the listed trim and equipment where that can be confirmed.

not_for_you_block.headline: Who this may not suit
items: If you need a roomy rear seat and maximum luggage space, a C-HR can feel tighter than more square-backed compact SUVs.
If you want hybrid plus 4WD in the same C-HR, this range does not give you that combination, the hybrid is 2WD only.
If you are set on the newer-shape overseas C-HR, a 2023 import from Japan is not that car.
